dataset: Apollo 204: 1967 Review Board versus contemporary NASA response
board_document: Apollo 204 Review Board report Part VI (1967)
response_document: Excerpt from 30 January 1968 Senate committee report, reproduced on NASA's website
policy: No NASA photographs, no inferred modern compliance, no NASA endorsement; primary-source links only

records.title: Oxygen tests reclassified
records.board_summary: The Board treated the pure-oxygen atmosphere as a severe fire hazard and called for full-scale testing and further study of diluent gas.
records.response_locator: Procedures, item 1; One Hundred Percent Pure Oxygen Environment
records.response_summary: The later NASA account says pure-oxygen tests were reclassified as hazardous and launch-pad command-module systems were changed, while atmosphere tradeoffs remained under evaluation.
records.status: Contemporary measures reported; this does not certify every test condition or a final flight atmosphere.

records.title: Combustible material controls
records.board_summary: The Board demanded tighter control of the quantity and placement of combustible material in the command module.
records.response_summary: NASA subsequently reported significant restrictions on the selection and placement of combustible materials.
records.status: The historical report describes a change as instituted; it does not inspect every later installation.

records.title: Crew escape and the hatch
records.board_summary: The Board found that cabin pressure prevented inner-hatch escape before rupture and recommended faster, simpler egress.
records.response_locator: Spacecraft and Facility Modifications, items 3 and 6
records.response_summary: The subsequent account described a quick-opening hatch as being developed for Block II spacecraft and launch-facility changes already made.
records.status: A hatch being developed was not yet proof of installation or operational qualification.

records.title: Rescue equipment and practice
records.board_summary: The Board urged regular emergency preparation, suitable rescue equipment and safer access routes.
records.response_locator: Procedures, item 4; Spacecraft and Facility Modifications, item 6
records.response_summary: NASA later described requirements for support-personnel emergency training and pad rescue equipment, and modified launch facilities.
records.status: A requirement is not evidence that every future team successfully passed a readiness exercise.

records.title: Independent safety review
records.board_locator: Part VI, Findings 5 and 11 and recommendations
records.board_summary: The Board identified failures of hazardous-test recognition, oversight and responsibility coordination.
records.response_summary: The response said test-procedure responsibility had been redefined and an independent Office of Flight Safety established.
records.status: The excerpt reports organization changes rather than measuring long-term safety outcomes.

records.title: Fire protection and emergency oxygen
records.board_summary: The Board called for improved fire control, extinguishing capability and auxiliary oxygen to protect against smoke and toxic gases.
records.response_summary: The later NASA account described provision for a jellied-water fire-extinguishing capability and emergency crew oxygen.
records.status: Provision in a historical response is not proof of final configuration or successful in-flight operation.
